title: Please claim also `podman.exe` in Bash completion script
body:
### Issue Description

podman bash completion should claim `podman` and `podman.exe`.
If you use Podman from Git Bash on Windows, the command might complete to `podman.exe` and then the completion done by `source <(podman completion bash)` does not trigger.
A work-around is to do `source <(podman completion bash | sed 's/podman$/podman podman.exe/')`, but it would be nice if the generated completion script would right away cover both options.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

- Set up Bash completion as documented
- Try to complete after `podman.exe `

### Describe the results you received

No completion

### Describe the results you expected

Completion

comments.body:
There is already a history about https://github.com/containers/podman/issues/16499 in there.
This is by design AFAICT. The completion scripts are generated by cobra, not us.
I can work on this issue and would be happy to `contribute`. Please `assign` it to me.

> This is by design AFAICT.

Then the design is wrong. :-)
In Git Bash you can do `podman <TAB>` or `podman.exe <TAB>` and if you did `podma<TAB>` you end up with `podman.exe` and then cannot use completion unless you delete the extension first or fixed the completion script.

> The completion scripts are generated by cobra, not us.

Then I would kindly ask that you bring up the issue upstream.
I don't know what cobra is and am not involved with it.
I'm using podman and used the documented way to set up the completion and it doesn't work as expected. :-)

https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1853#issuecomment-1597459009

per that it sounds like wontfix

we switched the command name to strip .exe for other uses who wanted the completion for the name without exe. We can only define one name as root command so it is a either choice podman has and the call was made to strip it.

As I noted on the PR I do not want to mess with the script directly since we do not generate and must not rely on implementation details. So either you get upstream convinced or we wont have it as far as I am concerned
